title: Concentrating six particles
hook: Keep the solute; change the space it occupies.

knows: Concentration compares the amount of solute with the volume of solution.
doesNotKnow: How changing volume with fixed solute changes average concentration.

objective: Relate concentration to the ratio of solute amount to solution volume in a particle model.

claims.text: Question, stage and reveal: A model solution has 6 solute particles in 3 equal-volume compartments. You remove water until the volume is 2 compartments, without losing solute. Once evenly mixed, how many particles per compartment on average? The same 6 particles occupy 2 equal compartments, so the average is 6 ÷ 2 = 3 per compartment. The dots are a counting model; real particles move and are not fixed in compartments.
The compartments are equal-volume counting regions, not physical barriers; the particles represent a simplified evenly mixed model.
When the amount of solute is unchanged, doubling the solution volume halves its concentration.

recall.question: You double a solution’s volume by adding solvent, keeping all solute. What happens to its concentration?
recall.why: Concentration is amount divided by volume; the same amount in twice the volume gives half the concentration.
